answer: One defence is a work-priced admission ticket: before an agent can trade, it must complete a unique, time-locked verifiable computation tied to its public key. In an orchard of would-be sellers, a single operator who plants a thousand fake identities must pay the compute cost a thousand times, while honest agents pay it once. The shale layer of the ledger records each ticket permanently, so reused or forged tickets are rejected instantly, and a raven-style random audit samples agents and revokes tickets whose work does not verify, making mass fakery expensive and unprofitable.
